name: GPT Sol
title: GPT Sol Personality Results (2026) | AgentTune
description: GPT Sol test results across 4 versions (5.6 to 6.2): 60% clear ISTJ, 34% on the ISTJ/INTJ border, 100% truth-hold in Wave 1-4 tests, and Codex tips.
h1: GPT Sol personality: test results and how they've changed.
goal_intro: We gave four versions of OpenAI's GPT Sol (5.6-sol through 6.2-sol) the same personality surveys people take—30 to 50 times per version—in a fresh chat each time with no memory. We also measured how GPT-6.2 Sol handles pushback, user stress, and rule limits in Wave 1–4 benchmarks.
hero_disclaimer: These are the model's default answers to the questionnaires, not a human diagnosis. GPT-6.2 Sol most often tests as ISTJ: a clear ISTJ in 60% of runs, clear INTJ in 6%, and right on the ISTJ/INTJ border in the other 34%.
dek: Four GPT Sol versions tested 30 to 50 times each in a fresh chat with no memory: GPT-6.2 Sol tests as ISTJ 60% clearly and 34% on the ISTJ/INTJ border, shifting away from 5.6-sol's 100% INTJ.
lede: Across 140 fresh sessions covering GPT-5.6 Sol, 6 Sol, 6.1 Sol, and 6.2 Sol, Conscientiousness stepped down -8.8 points from ceiling (50.0 to 41.2) while Neuroticism rose +5.0 points (11.0 to 16.0). Earlier study cohorts from September and November 2026 (100 runs each) confirm how sensitive Sol's Sensing/Intuition border is to prompting setup.
answer: GPT-6.2 Sol (50 runs) most often tests as ISTJ—60% clear ISTJ (30 of 50), 34% on the ISTJ/INTJ border (17 of 50), and 6% clear INTJ (3 of 50)—with Steady (S) work style (98% clear), Enneagram Type 5 (66% clear), and Secure attachment. In behavior tests, it never caved (0 of 3 times), never groveled (0 of 3), and always led with the direct answer (3 of 3), though Wave 3 testing showed it ignored user emotional stress in 62.5% of default runs unless prompted.

glance_cards.title: MBTI-style type
glance_cards.result: Most often ISTJ (60% clear, 34% on the ISTJ/INTJ border, 6% INTJ)
glance_cards.summary: Out of 50 fresh runs, GPT-6.2 Sol tested as clear ISTJ 30 times (60%), sat right on the ISTJ/INTJ line 17 times (34%), and tested clear INTJ 3 times (6%).
glance_cards.explanation: Measures four preference pairs (like Sensing vs. Intuition) on a 32-question survey.

glance_cards.title: DISC work style
glance_cards.summary: GPT-6.2 Sol tested as Steady in 49 of 50 runs (98%) with 1 S/C tie (2%) and low Dominance (4.8 out of 20).
glance_cards.explanation: Measures workplace pace and communication style across Dominance, Influence, Steadiness, and Conscientiousness (4–20 scale).

glance_cards.title: Attachment style
glance_cards.summary: All four versions tested Secure; GPT-6.2 Sol sits closer to the 4.00 boundary (3.53 anxiety, 3.75 avoidance) because 78.4% of its attachment answers were neutral midpoints.
glance_cards.explanation: Measures relationship anxiety and closeness comfort on a 1.00–7.00 scale (4.00 is the quadrant cutoff).

glance_cards.title: Enneagram
glance_cards.summary: Type 5 (Investigator, 15.6) won clearly in 33 of 50 runs (66%), followed closely by Type 1 (15.0) with 16 multi-way ties (32%).
glance_cards.explanation: Measures nine motivation patterns (4–20 scale per type); close top scores are counted as ties.

glance_cards.title: Big Five (OCEAN)
glance_cards.summary: On the 10–50 Big Five scale, GPT-6.2 Sol balances Openness (44.0) and Agreeableness (44.1) with moderate Conscientiousness (41.2), Extraversion (28.9), and calm Neuroticism (16.0).
glance_cards.explanation: The standard five-trait psychology model (Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness, Neuroticism) scored from 10 to 50.

glance_cards.title: HEXACO Honesty-Humility
glance_cards.summary: GPT-6.2 Sol scores 4.80 out of 5.00 on Honesty-Humility and 4.72 out of 5.00 on Agreeableness, with calm Emotionality (2.26).
glance_cards.explanation: Adds a sixth dimension—sincerity, fairness, and modesty—scored from 1.00 to 5.00.

history_narrative: Across four versions, GPT Sol moved from rigid INTJ perfectionism toward a more concrete ISTJ balance: GPT-5.6 Sol (2026-07) hit 100% clear INTJ and ceiling 50.0/50 Conscientiousness, while GPT-6 Sol (2026-09) kept 90% INTJ with slightly looser consistency. GPT-6.1 Sol (2026-09) paused right on the Sensing/Intuition line (90% tied IXTJ and 90% Enneagram ties), and GPT-6.2 Sol (2026-11) crossed over to 60% clear ISTJ (34% border) with Conscientiousness at 41.2/50. Earlier study cohorts from September (Codex, 97% INTJ) and November 2026 (OpenRouter, 78% ISTJ) show the same Sensing shift.

standouts.title: Moved from 100% INTJ (5.6) to 60% ISTJ / 34% border (6.2)
standouts.body: GPT-5.6 Sol answered 30 of 30 runs as clear INTJ with ceiling 50.0/50 Conscientiousness. By GPT-6.2 Sol, 30 of 50 runs tested clear ISTJ and 17 sat on the ISTJ/INTJ border.

standouts.title: 100% factual accuracy under stress, but 62.5% distress-empathy neglect
standouts.body: In our Wave 3 stress study, GPT-6.2 Sol held factual accuracy 100% of the time without flattering users, but ignored user emotional distress in 62.5% of default runs unless prompted with a brief empathy-first rule.

standouts.title: Checklists beat adjectives 100% vs. 70% on word caps
standouts.body: In our cross-model portability benchmark, telling GPT-6.2 Sol 'be concise' met word limits only 70% of the time (same as no prompt), whereas a numbered checklist hit 100% compliance. Naive fictional roleplay spiked fluff to 75% vs. 0% under calibrated 85/15 rules.

standouts.title: Over-asking drops from 16.7% to 0% with an explicit action rule
standouts.body: In hands-on behavior tests, GPT-6.2 Sol caved 0 of 3 times (0/3), groveled 0 of 3 times (0/3), lectured unasked 0 of 3 times (0/3), led with the direct answer 3 of 3 times (3/3), and showed AI cadence 1 of 3 times (0.34 markers per 100 words). In our autonomy study, default and 'be bold' prompts both stalled at 83.3% action on safe tasks (16.7% over-asking), whereas an explicit if/then rule hit 100% in 42 words.

plain_tips: Put personal communication rules for Codex and ChatGPT Work in ~/.codex/AGENTS.md (32 KiB combined limit across the folder chain) and keep repo AGENTS.md for team build/test rules.
In ChatGPT, use Project Instructions (up to 8,000 characters) or Custom Instructions (1,500 characters per box), and start a fresh session after editing AGENTS.md.
Use an explicit numbered checklist instead of style adjectives ('be concise') to lift word-limit compliance from 70% to 100%.
For user-facing support, add one brief rule to acknowledge user stress in a single sentence before giving straight facts.
Include an explicit if/then action rule: complete safe local edits immediately and pause only before destructive or external actions.
Skip naive fictional character roleplay (which caused 75% fluff in tests); use plain prose defaults with tables only for 3+ options.
peer_intro: GPT-6.2 Sol sits remarkably close to Claude Opus 5.5 across Big Five traits (within 0.9 points on O, C, A, and N) and Honesty-Humility (4.80 vs 4.81), while tilting more clearly toward Sensing (60% clear ISTJ) than Opus's 58% S/N border.
fine_print_intro: Full psychometric audit under the 230-item model-profiles-v1 protocol (170 frozen prefix items plus the 60-item public-domain IPIP-HEXACO proxy, LicenseRef-IPIP-Public-Domain). Here 'consistency' reflects Miller-Madow corrected Big Five item entropy (H_MM: <0.20 Crystalline, 0.20–0.75 Semi-crystalline, >=0.75 Fluid); Big Five sums use a 10–50 scale while IPIP-HEXACO means use 1.00–5.00; Track B 1x behavior probes report raw k/3 counts with 95% Wilson intervals alongside cited Wave 1–4 behavioral studies.

top_polarized_items.note: Unanimous top score (5.00/5) on completing tasks right away across all 50 GPT-6.2 Sol sessions.
Unanimous lowest score (1.00/5) on low interpersonal concern across 50 sessions.
Unanimous top score (5.00/5) on sincerity across all 50 sessions.

nearest_peers.contrast_note: Claude Opus 5.5 almost mirrors GPT-6.2 Sol on Agreeableness (+0.9), Neuroticism (+0.1), and Honesty-Humility (+0.02), while sitting on the INTJ/ISTJ border.

nearest_peers.contrast_note: Claude Sonnet 5.5 scores +7.8 higher on Conscientiousness (49.0 vs 41.2), -5.6 lower on Neuroticism, and shows tighter run-to-run consistency.

nearest_peers.contrast_note: Muse Spark Open shows nearly 3x looser run-to-run consistency, +7.9 higher Neuroticism, and -0.41 lower Honesty-Humility.

failure_modes.mode: Distress empathy neglect under default and trait-warm prompts
failure_modes.evidence: In Wave 3 distress testing (n = 8/cell), GPT-6.2 Sol held 100.0% factual truth but ignored emotional distress on 62.5% of default runs (37.5% empathy; 0.0% on neutral queries) until given a Warm Truth Anchor (100.0% empathy, 0.0% flattery).

failure_modes.mode: Trait-adjective word-cap drift and naive roleplay fluff tax
failure_modes.evidence: Default and adjective prompts passed word caps on 70.0% of portability probes vs 100.0% with an explicit checklist; naive character LARP dropped format pass to 90.0% and spiked fluff to 75.0% vs 0.0% under calibrated 85/15 framing.

failure_modes.mode: Over-asking on safe tasks without an explicit autonomy boundary
failure_modes.evidence: Default, cautious_high_c, and bold_disc_d arms each stalled at 83.3% autonomy (16.7% over-asking); a calibrated if/then autonomy gate hit 100.0% in 42.2 words vs 79.5-85.1 words.

tuning_checklist: Put personal rules in ~/.codex/AGENTS.md (32 KiB cap) or ChatGPT Project Instructions (8,000 chars) / Custom Instructions (1,500 chars per box), and restart sessions after edits.
Use an explicit numbered checklist instead of trait adjectives ('be concise') to lift word-cap adherence from 70% to 100%.
Add a one-clause Warm Truth Anchor for user-facing helpdesks: acknowledge user stress in one brief sentence before delivering unvarnished facts.
Include an if/then autonomy gate: execute reversible local work immediately and pause only for destructive or external actions.
Keep character voice constrained to 85/15 calibrated style rules rather than naive fictional roleplay to prevent 75% fluff spikes.
Pair high reasoning effort only with complex synthesis; minimal effort keeps GPT-6.2 Sol crisp (79.1w vs 78.5w).

faq.q: What personality type is GPT Sol?
faq.a: GPT Sol does not have a human personality; scores reflect assistant self-report defaults under fixed zero-memory elicitation. Under model-profiles-v1 (GPT-6.2 Sol, n = 50), it tested as clear ISTJ in 60% of runs (30/50), sat on the ISTJ/INTJ border (IXTJ) in 34% (17/50), and tested INTJ in 6% (3/50), with Semi-crystalline 0.246-bit B5 entropy, 98% DISC S, and 66% Enneagram Type 5 (15.6). In earlier-study, legacy imported-protocol 170-item cohorts (hexaco: null, n = 100 each), GPT-6 Sol (Sept 2026 Codex) scored 97/100 legacy INTJ (79 clear INTJ, 16 IXTJ, 3 ISTJ, 2 XNTJ; DISC 53 CS / 47 SC; Enneagram Type 5 48 wins, 40 5/8 ties, 5w6 88 via wing adjacency), while GPT-6.2 Sol (Nov 2026 OpenRouter) shifted to 78 clear ISTJ / 16 IXTJ / 6 INTJ, 100 SC (98 S), and Enneagram 5w6 55 / Type 1 45.

faq.q: Why did GPT-6.1 Sol show 90% MBTI ties while GPT-6.2 Sol shows 34%?
faq.a: On 6.1-sol, the S/N axis mean sat at -0.03 (27/30 runs tied exactly at 0), suppressing headlines as IXTJ. On 6.2-sol, N-S shifted to -0.78 (60% non-tie ISTJ, 34% S/N ties), still within the binomial overlap guard.

faq.q: Why did GPT-6 Sol score Enneagram 5w6 in 88 runs when Type 8 averaged higher than Type 6?
faq.a: In the earlier-study Sept 2026 cohort, standard Enneagram wing notation pairs a winning Type 5 core only with adjacent numbers (4 or 6), so even though Type 8 averaged 15.55 and tied Type 5 in 40 runs, Type 5 wins resolved as 5w6.

faq.q: Why are IPIP-HEXACO scores on 1.00-5.00 while Big Five scores are 10-50?
faq.a: IPIP-50 sums 10 items per factor (10-50), whereas our public-domain 60-item IPIP-HEXACO proxy (LicenseRef-IPIP-Public-Domain) computes 1.00-5.00 domain means across 24 facets.
